create.name: Gaelyn Godwin
create.bio:
Gaelyn Godwin, whose dharma name is Setsuan Konjin, is a Soto Zen priest and the abbot and guiding teacher of Houston Zen Center in Texas. Her own training began at San Francisco Zen Center in 1985 and lasted eighteen years, twelve of them at Tassajara Zen Mountain Center in California, where she held many of the monastery's practice and work roles. She was ordained by Tenshin Reb Anderson in 1991 and received dharma transmission from him in 2003, in the lineage of Shunryu Suzuki. She also spent periods of training in Japan and with Robert Aitken in Hawaii, and in 2005 she was formally recognised as a teacher by the Soto school in Japan.

After several years of visiting to teach, she moved to Houston in 2003 to lead the centre. Her Sunday dharma talks often work closely through fascicles of Dogen's Shobogenzo, and she leads sesshin, intensive silent retreats, at Auspicious Cloud, the centre's rural retreat land in Chappell Hill. She has trained Zen priests and named several dharma heirs and lay teachers, leads a meditation group in a Texas prison, and has served as director of the international office of Soto Zen in North America and as president of the Soto Zen Buddhist Association.

courses.title: Rohatsu Sesshin 2026
courses.description: A five-day silent Zen retreat at Auspicious Cloud, Houston Zen Center's rural land in Chappell Hill, co-led with Zen priest Tim Schorre. Held each December in honour of the Buddha's awakening, it asks that participants have already sat at least one one-day sesshin; a weekend-only option is offered.

free_resources.description: An audio recording of a Sunday talk she gave at Houston Zen Center in October 2026, free to stream or download from the centre's talk archive and podcast.
